The follow-up distinguishes thinking it was the final target, knowingly leaving work unfinished, and uncertainty/mistaken selection. Correction follows the self-report, so it does not teach the distinction before that confirmation. The latter two choices have null hypotheses.

Unknown now admits forgotten reasoning or another approach without claiming no rule. Misclick explicitly allows intending the raised price and keeps only self-report evidence with null hypothesis. No forced same-base diagnosis remains in this response set.

Both feedback strings now explain the value relationship and explicitly state that the answer alone does not identify the method. The retained percent-as-pesos label is a possible hypothesis only, not confirmation; the new contract forbids knowledge updates and requires cause to remain uncertain where teaching preceded the response. Nulling that hypothesis would also be conservative but is not required by this assessment.

Both flows and contrast reference a contract requiring attempt/node/response/sequence/target and teaching/help provenance. It preserves the first unassisted response, marks subsequent same-item responses helped, forbids tutor-node knowledge updates, and forbids post-teaching self-report becoming pre-correction confirmation. The four previously problematic contrast nodes are now assisted_check and their correct responses have assisted_check evidence. Remaining possible hypotheses on wrong taught checks must remain uncertain by this contract. No current consumer or runtime enforcement is claimed.
